review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–114). It adds no simp lemmas, simp attributes or simp-set definitions. The five helper lemmas (exp_mul_exp, exp_neg_mul_exp, exp_mul_exp_neg, exp_neg_mul_exp_neg, conj_ofReal_mul_exp) are used only through explicit `rw`, in the h00, h10, h01 and h11 steps. Giving them `@[simp]` would be risky: their left sides are products of exponentials, and their right sides carry `((u+v : ℝ) : ℂ)` casts that the existing `push_cast`/`ofReal_add` simp lemmas would expand again. So I do not recommend it. The `simp`/`simpa` calls use explicit lemma lists (`Matrix.mul_apply`, `Fin.sum_univ_two`, `star_eq_conjTranspose`, `conjTranspose_apply`) and close their goals. The final `fin_cases` block runs a non-terminal `simp [...]` and then four `simpa using ...` bullets. That is somewhat fragile if the simp normal form changes. But I found no concrete competing rule, loop or missing canonical lemma to cite, and I did not run Lean. I did not inspect the Mathlib simp sets in depth, so I cannot rule out a minor issue there.
